facts.claim: DOE's FOA-2678 selectee fact sheet identified Microvast for a $200 million federal cost share alongside $304.54 million recipient cost share for a U.S. polyaramid-separator manufacturing project; DOE described Microvast as vertically integrated from core battery materials through battery packs and described the proposed separator facility as capable of supplying 19 GWh of EV batteries, alongside Microvast's existing 2 GWh Clarksville battery plant.

The same DOE record states that Microvast and General Motors intended to combine complementary intellectual property for a specialized separator and intended to use U.S.-sourced raw materials plus equipment manufactured in the U.S. or allied countries.

factors.name: crossDivisionLeverage
factors.basis: Independent DOE program documentation describes vertical integration spanning battery materials through packs and a planned separator collaboration with GM.

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: DOE documented an intended U.S. separator-manufacturing build using U.S.-sourced raw materials and U.S./allied equipment, supporting the localization thesis.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: DOE independently documented substantial planned separator capacity and an existing Clarksville plant, but this historical program record does not establish current utilization, completion, or present economics.

risks: The DOE source is a 2022 selectee/program record and should not be treated as proof that the proposed separator facility was completed, funded through final award, or is currently utilized.
Planned manufacturing capacity does not establish contracted demand, pricing power, or current return on invested capital.
unknowns: Current status of the 19 GWh separator project is not established by this source.
Current utilization and economics of Clarksville capacity are not established by this source.
This evidence does not provide current market valuation inputs.

confidence.basis: Independent U.S. Department of Energy program documentation directly identifies Microvast and provides project-level capacity, cost-share, integration and sourcing details; temporal limitations are explicit.
